---
title: "Serving software packages from the registry"
date: 2026-09-28
---

::: {.callout-note}
## Status: proposed, nothing started
A plan for making `bioconductor.org`'s software repositories come from
[bioc-registry](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-registry), which is built from r-universe,
instead of from the legacy build system (BBS). Every step and every test below cites the
measurement that makes it necessary. Measurements are from 2026-09-28 and are reproducible
with the scripts in
[`evidence/registry-switch/`](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/tree/main/evidence/registry-switch).
Tracked in [bioc-infrastructure#35](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/35).
:::

## Where software packages come from today

`bioconductor.org` is served by the new edge, but its package repositories are still an
hourly mirror of the legacy docroot. The Worker serves `/packages/...` from R2, which the
edge's sync job fills from that docroot. It never reads from the registry.

| On `bioconductor.org` | Sample | Built by |
|---|---|---|
| Release (3.23) source tarballs | 20 of 20 | BBS (packaged by `biocbuild`) |
| Devel (3.24) source tarballs | 10 of 10 | BBS (`biocbuild`) |
| Release Windows binaries | 15 of 15 | r-universe (carry r-universe's `RemoteSha`) |
| Release macOS binary (limma) | 1 | r-universe |

So Windows and macOS users already install r-universe builds, reaching `bioconductor.org`
through the core team's propagation, which only publishes an r-universe build whose version
and commit match what the BBS host `nebbiolo1` built ([legacy propagation](legacy-propagation.qmd)).
Anyone installing from source (Linux, most CI, containers) gets BBS tarballs.

Separately, the registry already runs a complete r-universe-built repository, gated by its own
[propagation gate](propagation-gate.qmd), at
`https://bioc-registry.seandavi.workers.dev/repo/{bioc-release,bioc}`. Nothing on
`bioconductor.org` uses it yet. Switching `bioconductor.org` to it is the step that takes BBS
out of the path for software packages.

## What the switch covers

| Path under `/packages/<ver>/bioc/` | After the switch | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `src/contrib/` tarballs and `PACKAGES`, `.gz`, `.rds` | registry | the install path |
| `bin/windows/…`, `bin/macosx/…` binaries and their indexes | registry | the install path |
| `VIEWS` | registry | read by BiocManager-adjacent tools and the site build |
| `src/contrib/Archive/` | stays on the mirror at first | old versions; the registry keeps none (see finding 5) |
| `vignettes/`, `news/`, `manuals/`, `licenses/`, `citations/`, `readmes/` | stays on the mirror | produced by BBS; the registry doesn't produce them |
| `html/` | unchanged (the site build) | |

Only the current release (3.23) and devel (3.24). Older releases are archival
([ADR 0006](adr/0006-old-releases-and-their-checkresults-are-archival.html)) and stay as they
are; they are 77% of package traffic, so most installs are unaffected either way. Annotation,
experiment and workflow repositories stay on the mirror until
[bioc-build](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-build) covers them.

## Findings: what would regress if we switched today

Compared file by file, the registry and `bioconductor.org` agree on almost everything: for
release, 2,374 of 2,384 source packages at the same version. The differences below are the
ones that matter. Request counts are from about 70 minutes of post-cutover access logs, with
a blocked crawler excluded.

**1. No `PACKAGES.rds`.** The registry serves `PACKAGES` and `PACKAGES.gz` but answers 404 for
`PACKAGES.rds`, for source and every binary directory. It's the index R asks for first, and
the most requested: 2,784 requests against about 220 for `.gz` and plain `PACKAGES`. R falls
back to the next format, so installs keep working, but every repository lookup pays an extra
round trip. *Blocking.*

**2. Packages that can't be installed.** The registry serves 6 release and 13 devel packages
that `bioconductor.org` doesn't, such as `Ularcirc`, `SNPhood`, `progeny` and `sparrow`. They
are still in Bioconductor's manifest and in r-universe, but a hard dependency was removed from
Bioconductor (`decoupleR`, `BiocSet`, `Organism.dplyr`, `BPRMeth`), so BBS stopped propagating
them. Checked with `tools::package_dependencies` over the repository plus CRAN and the data
repositories, the registry adds 4 release and 7 devel packages whose hard dependencies can't
be resolved, on top of `bioconductor.org`'s own (9 release, 2 devel, all CRAN packages that
were archived). A user asking for one gets a confusing failure instead of "not available".
*Blocking.* The fix is a gate rule, not a list: don't publish a package whose hard
dependencies aren't resolvable.

**3. Frozen seeded packages.** 153 release and 124 devel entries were seeded once from
Bioconductor's own builds for packages that fail in r-universe's environment, and seeds never
update. Today 3 release and 6 devel seeds are behind `bioconductor.org`, including `biomaRt`,
`DOSE` and `CNVRanger`; two devel packages propagated by the gate are behind as well
(`PIPETS` at 1.7.0 against 1.9.0). After a switch, bug-fix releases of those packages would
stop reaching users. *Blocking*, until either the packages build in r-universe or seeds are
refreshed while BBS still produces them. Refreshing seeds keeps BBS in the path for those
packages, so it's a bridge, not an end state.

**4. Missing binaries.** For release, the registry lacks 61 Windows, 49 macOS arm64 and 76
macOS Intel binaries that `bioconductor.org` serves (devel: 48, 57, 72). The sampled ones are
r-universe builds, so the registry didn't propagate binaries that exist. Without them, Windows
and macOS users get a source install, which fails for any package with compiled code on a
machine without a toolchain. *Blocking.*

**5. No `Archive/`.** The registry keeps only the current version. `src/contrib/Archive/` on
`bioconductor.org` served 886 requests (renv restores and `remotes::install_version`) in the
sample. At first it stays on the mirror; once BBS stops producing it, superseded registry
tarballs have to be archived by whatever writes the repository. *Blocking for detaching BBS,
not for the switch.*

**6. Data and workflow packages in the software repository.** The registry has two
universes, `bioc` and `bioc-release`, and bioc-build publishes into them, so `msdata`
(experiment data), `rnaseqDTU` (a workflow) and `ARRmData` appear in the software `PACKAGES`.
*Blocking.* They belong in `data/experiment` and `workflows`.

**7. Missing index fields.** `PACKAGES` lacks `MD5sum`, `Archs`, `License_is_FOSS` and
`License_restricts_use`; `VIEWS` lacks those plus `dependencyCount`, `Rfiles`, `hasNEWS`,
`organism`, `PackageStatus` and others. No consumer of `MD5sum` is confirmed. Writing the
indexes with R's `tools::write_PACKAGES()` from the actual tarballs produces the `PACKAGES`
fields for free. *Not blocking*; the `VIEWS` fields are checked against the site build.

**8. Same version, different build.** For 33 release packages both sides have the same
version but different contents: `bioconductor.org` declares `R (>= 4.6)`, the registry
`R (>= 4.5)`. The maintainer changed DESCRIPTION without a version bump, and the registry
kept the first build of that version, as its gate intends. Installing on R 4.6 is unaffected.
*Expected; the tests must allow it.*

**9. The registry is not built to serve at edge speed.** Its indexes are generated per
request with `cache-control: no-store` and take 250–550 ms; `bioconductor.org` serves the
same files from the edge cache in about 60–85 ms. The index changes a few times a day for
release and about ten times a day for devel. This decides the mechanism below.

## Mechanism: write the registry's repository into the edge's storage

Two ways to serve it:

- **Proxy**: the Worker forwards `/packages/3.2x/bioc/src/…` to the registry at request
  time. Every index request would take the registry's latency or need a new caching and purge
  scheme, and `bioconductor.org` installs would depend on the registry Worker being up.
- **Materialize** (recommended): a job writes the registry's repository into the same R2
  keys the mirror writes today (`packages/3.24/bioc/src/contrib/…`), generating
  `PACKAGES`, `.gz` and `.rds` with `tools::write_PACKAGES()` from the tarballs, and purges
  the changed keys with the existing `cf_purge_keys`. The Worker, its cache rules, 404
  caching, logs, and the mirror manifest need no change. The hourly sync stops writing those
  paths (an `rsync-filter` exclusion), and turning that exclusion off again is the rollback.

This follows the rule the estate already has: producers publish into storage, and the edge
decides what to serve ([contract 3 on the overview](index.qmd#the-contracts)).

## Plan

Each step names its rollback. Nothing moves to the next step until its tests pass.

**0. Fix the blocking gaps in the registry.**

- Gate rule: a package is published only if its hard dependencies resolve within the
  repository, CRAN and the Bioconductor data repositories (finding 2).
- Binaries: propagate every r-universe binary that matches the published source version
  (finding 4).
- Repository type: route bioc-build output into data and workflow repositories, never the
  software index (finding 6).
- Seeds: a decision (finding 3). Either re-seed on a schedule from BBS as a bridge, or
  accept that those packages lag until they build in r-universe. As of today, 9 seeds lag.

**1. Build the materializer, writing to a staging prefix.** It writes the full software tree
for 3.23 and 3.24 under a prefix the Worker doesn't serve (for example `staging/registry/`),
on every registry index change. Rollback: nothing is served from it.

**2. Serve the staging tree on the rehearsal host.** `next.bioconductor.org` gets a route that
maps `/packages/3.2x/bioc/{src,bin,VIEWS}` to the staging prefix, the same mechanism as the
strangler route table. Run every test below against `next.` for at least a week of registry
updates. Rollback: remove the route.

**3. Flip devel (3.24) on `bioconductor.org`.** Devel is 2% of package traffic and its users
expect movement. The materializer writes the production keys for 3.24; the hourly sync
excludes them. Watch the logs for 404s and for installs of packages that used to exist. Hold
for a week. Rollback: remove the exclusion, run the sync, purge.

**4. Flip release (3.23).** Same steps, after devel has been clean for a week. Rollback:
same.

**5. Archive.** Before BBS stops producing `Archive/`, the materializer moves superseded
tarballs into `Archive/<pkg>/` (finding 5).

After step 4, BBS is out of the install path for software packages, except for any seeds
that are still bridged (finding 3). The legacy docroot still supplies documentation files
and older releases until M2 retires it.

## Regression tests

Each test exists because of a finding above. The comparison tests use `bioconductor.org` as
the baseline while BBS still runs; after the flip their baseline becomes the previous
materialized state.

| # | Test | Guards against | Runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Every package in the baseline is present at the same or a newer version | missing or older packages (findings 3, 6) | on every materialize; blocks publishing |
| T2 | No package whose hard dependencies are unresolvable, beyond the baseline's own | uninstallable packages (finding 2) | on every materialize; blocks |
| T3 | `PACKAGES`, `.gz` and `.rds` exist in every directory and parse to the same package set | missing index formats (finding 1) | on every materialize; blocks |
| T4 | For each platform, binaries cover the baseline's binaries at the matching version | Windows/macOS falling back to source (finding 4) | on every materialize; blocks |
| T5 | Every tarball's name matches its DESCRIPTION's `Package` and `Version`, and its hash matches the registry index | corrupt or mislabeled artifacts | on every materialize; blocks |
| T6 | No data or workflow package in the software index | repository-type mix-up (finding 6) | on every materialize; blocks |
| T7 | `BiocManager::install()` for release and devel, from source on Linux and from binaries on Windows and macOS, for a fixed sample including packages with compiled code | an install path that parses but doesn't work | CI matrix, daily and before each flip |
| T8 | A package's previous version installs from `Archive/` | breaking renv and `install_version` (finding 5) | daily after step 5 |
| T9 | After a registry propagation, `bioconductor.org` serves the new `PACKAGES` within one materialize cycle | a stale edge cache (s-maxage is a year) | on every materialize |
| T10 | Same-version differences (finding 8) are reported, not failed | noise that would train everyone to ignore T1 | reported daily |

T1–T6 and T9 are checks on files the materializer just wrote, so they run inside it and stop
it from publishing a broken tree. T7 already exists in part
(`test-biocmanager.R` in bioc-edge, which passes for 3.23 and 3.24 against
`bioconductor.org` today) and needs Windows and macOS runners.

## Decisions needed

- **Seeds** (finding 3): bridge from BBS for now, or let those packages lag?
- **Mirror operators** keep syncing from the legacy host, so after the flip they would serve
  BBS builds while `bioconductor.org` serves registry builds. Point them at the manifest-based
  [mirror guide](mirror-how-to.qmd) first, or accept the divergence for a while?
- **Documentation files** (`vignettes/` and the rest) stay on BBS's output, so for a package
  where the two builds differ, its vignette can come from a different build than its tarball.
  Acceptable until the site build produces them?
